encounter.reason: Acute Anterior STEMI with critical troponin elevation

documents.title: Emergency Department Admission Note
documents.content:
## Patient: Sarah, 38yo cis-male

**HPI:** Acute anterior STEMI presenting with chest pain, diaphoresis, ST elevation V1-V4, catheterization performed.  Patient reports significant distress and rapid onset of symptoms.

**Physical Exam:** Vital signs stable, but exhibiting signs of anxiety and respiratory distress. Auscultation reveals crackles in the right lower lobe. Skin appears pale and cool.

**Management Plan:** Immediate initiation of intravenous fluids (lactated ringers) to address hypotension and potential fluid overload.  Oxygen supplementation with high-flow nasal cannula. Continuous cardiac monitoring with serial troponin levels. Reserved for emergent PCI based on evolving clinical presentation and troponin trends.  Continue supportive care, including pain management and anxiety reduction.

diagnostics.conclusion: Cardiac Troponin I abnormal findings: Acute Anterior STEMI with critical troponin elevation. Key indicators: chest pain, diaphoresis.
